minutes_text:
CITY OF BEVERLY HILLS
  455 North Rexford Drive
  Beverly Hills, CA 90210
  Video Teleconference
  Beverly Hills City Council Liaison / Priority Setting Ad Hoc Committee Meeting

  SPECIAL MEETING HIGHLIGHTS

  Tuesday, July 9, 2024
  1:00 PM

MEETING CALLED TO ORDER
Date / Time:  July 9, 2024 / 1:00 PM
IN ATTENDANCE:  Vice Mayor Sharona Nazarian, Councilmember Craig Corman, City
  Manager Nancy Coffey, Assistant City Manager Ryan Gohlich, Municipal
  Affairs Program Manager Cynthia Owens

  1) Public Comment:

  None

  2) Auditor Discussion with Audit Committee:
  a. Presentation by Nancy Coffey:
  i. In 2023 the council laid out 45 priorities for the city.
  ii. These priorities are a mixture of work plans, goals, and aspirations.
  iii. Priorities are not always timebound, measurable, or action oriented.
  iv. Creating the list of City Council Priorities for the upcoming year is usually
  done in April, when the budget for the same period is mostly done, which
  can leave the two disconnected.
  v. Three different approaches to priorities were then presented. The first was
  from Tracey, CA; the second was from Corona, CA; and the final was from
  Montpelier, VT.
  vi. Staff is requesting council direction on whether they should create an
  overarching umbrella list of priorities that guide the City’s workplan,
  whether they should engage is a planning process to inform the priorities,
  whether they should make all priorities achievable, measurable, and action
  oriented, and whether the timing of the priority setting session should occur
  at a different time of year.
  b. Councilmember Corman is concerned about using public facing percentage bars
  to measure priorities, as they are easily manipulated by placing several easily
  accomplished items in the mix to distort the true nature of how much work needs
  to be done.
  c. Councilmember Corman is in favor of tiering priorities from macro items to
  individual workplans.
  d. He also feels that the way that the city currently does priorities is flawed and is
  poorly organized between necessary items and aspirational goals.
  e. He also agrees with moving the priority setting session to more closely align with
  the budget so that they can be connected to each other.
 Highlights for July 9, 2024
Priority Setting Ad Hoc Committee

  f. He also believes that comprehensive plans such as the complete streets plan
  should be treated separately from overarching goals and that they should have a
  scheduling document to guide the implementation of the plan.
  g. Vice Mayor Nazarian is also in favor of tiering priorities.
  h. The Vice Mayor believes that preliminary discussions about the priority setting
  session should happen around October or November, so that they are fully
  discussed and planned, so that staff can quickly move to implement them once
  they are fully adopted in April.
  i. She also stated that one of the umbrella items should be focused on Mayoral
  initiatives that the Mayor believes the city should focus on during their year in the
  position.
  j. The Vice Mayor also wants a check in with the Council, City Manager, and the
  department heads during the year for an update on what steps they have taken to
  implement their assigned priorities and to ensure clear communication between
  the various departments working on the plans.
  k. She also believes that workplans should be flexible to allow for changes to be
  made as things come up during the year.
  l. The Vice Mayor would also like for all the events the city department are planning
  and their respective funding requests to be presented during the priority setting
  session so that the Council can make an informed decision about the budgets of
  various events instead of approving them piecemeal throughout the year.
  m. The City Manager brought up the idea of bringing a quarterly update on the
  priorities to the Council, like what currently happens with the budget.
  n. Councilmemebr Corman likes the rigidity that comes with a strategic plan as it
  would make Council and Staff more disciplined when approaching issues as they
  would both have a set of ranked priorities rather than an unprioritized set of
  priorities and council directions that may or may not conflict with each other.
  o. He is in favor of having a special umbrella item for Mayor initiatives.
  p. Councilmember Corman is in favor of having a midyear update to Council about
  city priorities rather than a quarterly update which he believes to be too short term.
  q. This will come before the full council on August 6th.

  3) Adjournment:
  Date / Time: July 9, 2024 / 1:45 PM
